record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.original_question: For zero-dimensional subsets X of the real line R, characterize when the countable power X^omega is homogeneous.

evidence.quote: Problem 4. For which 0-dimensional subsets X of R is Xω homogeneous? CDH?
The first part of this problem was answered by Lawrence [55], and further extended by Dow and Pearl [21]

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space Y is called homogeneous if for any two points y_1, y_2 in Y there exists a homeomorphism h: Y → Y with h(y_1) = y_2. A subspace X of the real line R is said to be zero-dimensional if it has a base consisting of clopen subsets. Endow X^ω, the countable Cartesian power of X with the product topology.

Problem: Give a characterization of those zero-dimensional subsets X ⊆ R for which the countable power X^ω is homogeneous.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is resolved. L. B. Lawrence proved that the ω-power of every subset of the Cantor set is homogeneous, and Dow and Pearl extended this by showing that every zero-dimensional first-countable T_0 space has a homogeneous ω-power. Since every subset of R is first-countable, X^ω is homogeneous for every zero-dimensional X ⊆ R.

status_evidence.title: Homogeneity in powers of zero-dimensional first-countable spaces (Dow–Pearl)
status_evidence.snippet: A construction of L. B. Lawrence is extended to show that the ω-power of every subset of the Cantor set is homogeneous; it follows that every zero-dimensional first-countable space has a homogeneous ω-power.
status_evidence.claim: Every zero-dimensional first-countable space (in particular every zero-dimensional subset of R) has homogeneous ω-power.

status_evidence.title: Topological homogeneity and infinite powers (Medini)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey citing Lawrence and Dow–Pearl: X^ω is homogeneous whenever X is zero-dimensional and first-countable.
status_evidence.claim: The first part of the problem is settled by the Lawrence and Dow–Pearl theorems.
